text:
oliver: onboarding PR for the python sample-app is failing on M1 macs in CI. pip tries to install redwood-sdk and pulls macosx_12_0_universal2 wheel, but our local dev machines are getting macosx_11_0_arm64 and then tests error out with ImportError for _fasttokenizer. anyone know why different wheel tags show up?

`tanya`: can you paste the pip output and the install command?

oliver: CI does `python -m pip install .[dev]` inside the macos runner. snippet: 

```
Downloading redwood_sdk-0.4.2-cp311-cp311-macosx_12_0_universal2.whl
Installing collected packages: redwood-sdk
  Attempting to build from source for redwood-sdk
  ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
ImportError: cannot import name '_fasttokenizer' from 'redwood_sdk._c_ext' (/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_sdk/_c_ext.cpython-311-darwin.so)
```

`rick`: two things here: 1) universal2 vs arm64 wheels can coexist; pip chooses based on many factors (wheel tags, platform, ABI). 2) the ImportError suggests either we shipped a wheel built for x86_64 and Rosetta translated it (or not), or there was a partial fallback where pip wrote a .so for a different arch.

`tanya`: did you build the wheel yourself or are we pulling from PyPI/private index?

oliver: CI pulls from our internal artifact index (artifactory). The publish job uploads two wheels: one tagged macosx_12_0_universal2 and one macosx_11_0_arm64. I double-checked both are present.

`devex-bot`: FYI: mac runners on GH actions use macos-12/x86_64 or macos-12/arm64 depending on the runner selection. Check matrix.

`oliver`: ah, our matrix had `runs-on: macos-12` but we didn't pin `arch`. GH picked an x86 runner for some jobs, arm64 for others. so CI sometimes installs the universal2 wheel (works on both), sometimes the arm64 wheel. but the ImportError persisted on arm64 runs.

`rick`: ImportError hints the C-extension wasn't built with the right flags or the wheel is missing the compiled module for that tag. Could be our sdist build pipeline only produced universal2 and we uploaded a broken arm64 wheel (maybe it was an empty artifact). Can you `pip download` the wheel in CI and inspect with `file` and `tar -tf`?

oliver: did that locally: `file redwood_sdk-0.4.2-cp311-cp311-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl` -> shows `Mach-O 64-bit object arm64`. `unzip -l` shows `_c_ext.cpython-311-darwin.so` present. sizes look small (~20k).

`tanya`: small size is suspicious. our _fasttokenizer .so should be > 1MB. Looks like the build of the wheel used a stub or stripped artifact. How do we build wheels in the publish job?

oliver`: we run `python -m build` inside a Docker image that cross-compiles with cibuildwheel on a linux runner and then upload. we had a recent change to the wheel builder config to enable mac universal builds using `delocate` and `cibuildwheel` but I bet something broke in the arm64 path.

`rick`: cibuildwheel cross-building mac wheels from linux isn't supported. You must build mac wheels on mac runners (or use manylinux for linux). If your pipeline tried to run delocate on linux, the produced artifact probably doesn't contain actual arm64 .so — maybe it dropped the binary and left a stub. That explains small size.

`tanya`: two recommended fixes:
- move mac wheel builds to mac runners (use a `build-macos` job) so arm64/universal2 are properly built.
- or publish only universal2 built on mac and make sure artifact is the expected size. For CI, as a stop-gap, pin the sample-app to install the pure-python wheel (if exists) or run `pip install --no-binary=:all: redwood-sdk` and build from source on the runner (requires Xcode & rust for some deps though).

oliver`: we do require rust for the tokenizer crate. building from source on GH mac runners requires installing `rustup` and setting env vars — not great for onboarding speed. we prefer prebuilt wheels.

`devex-bot`: Suggestion: add a deployment check job that downloads each published wheel and runs `python -c "import platform, subprocess; print(platform.machine())"` inside a temp venv on matching runners to verify binary import.

`rick`: also check that `cibuildwheel` was invoked with `--output-dir` and that the publisher uploaded the correct files (not the sdist or a placeholder). our upload step used a glob `dist/*` — if artifacts on builder were mixed, a wrong file could be uploaded.

`oliver`: yep — found the bug: our linux builder produced the universal wheel using a fallback script that created a placeholder .so (to satisfy packaging) when it couldn't compile. the publish job didn't validate artifact sizes and uploaded both. copying to fix branch now.

`tanya`: long-term: maintain a tiny `verify-wheel` script in infra that checks `file`, size > 200kb, and attempt `python -c "import importlib; importlib.import_module('redwood_sdk._c_ext')"` inside a short venv on each platform. Add to release checklist.

`oliver`: pushing publish fix and adding quick check to release pipeline. opening ENG-4599 to track the verify script and updating sample-app README to note that devs on mac M1 should use the artifact index instead of building from source.

`ci-bot`: build 721 on branch fix/publish-wheels: macos-arm64 job passed, macos-x64 passed :white_check_mark:

`oliver`: thanks all. lesson: don't try to fake mac wheels from linux. marking resolved. :rocket:
